STATUS: fail
SUMMARY: One reproduced blocking bug: when a light-DOM target is slotted into a shadow tree, the shadow wrapper that composes it (the `<slot>`'s ancestor) gets `aria-hidden`, so the target sits inside a hidden subtree. The other shadow scenarios I probed (17 + 6 probes) hold, and the flag-off path matches HEAD. The overlays suite passes (the SSR suite passes under `yarn test:ssr`).
FILES TOUCHED: none (scratch probes `zz_probe.test.js` / `zz_probe3.test.js` were created and deleted; `git status` shows the same 4 modified files as before)
FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Slotted target hides its composed ancestor. `nodeContains` walks light `parentNode`s and never follows a slotted target's `assignedSlot`, so a `role="dialog"` wrapper that contains `<slot>` is treated as not containing the target and gets hidden. Repro: host in body with shadow `[button, div[role=dialog] > slot]`, light `input` child of host, `ariaHideOutside([input])` → `wrap.getAttribute('aria-hidden')` = `"true"`. Flag-off HEAD leaves it visible. The spec never names slots, so whether this is in scope is an open question (see below).
- [minor] Closed shadow roots are not walked: sibling inside a `mode:'closed'` target root stays unhidden (`s` had no aria-hidden). ShadowTreeWalker reads `host.shadowRoot`, which is null for closed roots. Spec does not mention closed roots.
- [minor] Element moved from a hidden sibling into the target keeps its stale `aria-hidden="true"` (reproduced). Same logic as the light-DOM observer (visible container → skip), so not a regression.
CHECKS:
- P1 sibling host content: only host hidden, inner not, restored → pass
- P2 target is a host: light sibling hidden, host/content visible → pass
- P3 row sibling in shadow root: cells hidden → pass
- P4 announcer in sibling host before call: announcer visible, host skipped, other content hidden → pass
- P5 nested wrapper+announcer appended to enclosing root → pass
- P6 element moved from target to shadow sibling → hidden → pass
- P7 two calls in different roots, out-of-order revert, re-observe → pass
- P8 revert after target host removed from document → pass, no throw
- P9 custom root inside shadow root (siblings outside root not hidden, late appends outside root not hidden) → pass
- P10 custom light root not containing host → pass
- P11 target host content appended later stays visible → pass
- P12 later-added host in enclosing root: host hidden, its content not → pass
- P13 keepVisible in shadow root, child of kept element → pass
- P14 three-level nesting, appends at every level incl. light → pass
- P15 pre-existing aria-hidden sibling survives revert → pass
- I1/I2 inert variants (sibling host inner not inert, late content not inert, restored) → pass
- Q3 double revert doesn't throw → pass; Q4 3000 shadow siblings hidden in ~60ms → pass; Q6 announcer appended inside target host's shadow root → pass
- F0/F1/F2/F3 flag off: default off; host and sibling unhidden matching HEAD (verified by running HEAD source); late light sibling hidden; late shadow content not observed; light row cells hidden → pass
- `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays` → 201/202 pass; the only failure (`useModal.ssr.test.js`) came from my override of the ignore pattern; `yarn test:ssr packages/@react-aria/overlays` → pass
- Probes I wrote that were wrong and not findings: Q5 (second call hides first call's target in the same root, which is correct), F1 (host not hidden with flag off, same as HEAD)
OPEN QUESTIONS: Is slotted content (light child rendered through `<slot>`) in scope? If yes, the bug above blocks; if no, record it as a known gap. Is closed-root support required?
